rows.evidence: Q1: Sections II-III; the authors measured leaf reflectance (350-2500 nm, ASD leaf clip) of 60 detached winter wheat leaves with visually estimated aphid densities (0-120 per leaf) at one experimental field in Beijing in May 2011, derived 48 spectral features, and fitted/validated a PLSR model (36 calibration, 24 validation leaves) giving R2 of 0.77 and RMSE of 15 (Fig. 6).
rows.notes: The study only shows that leaf-level hyperspectral features (including the Aphid Index among others) correlate with aphid density and that a PLSR model can estimate leaf aphid density. It does not identify affected areas of a crop (measurements are on detached leaves in a laboratory, not canopy or field mapping), and it reports nothing on farmers taking action or on preventing further damage. The authors themselves state that leaf-level analysis is only a first step and that upscaling to canopy/field level remains challenging. Hence the study supports only a precondition (detection) of the claimed pest-control effect; Q2 is 'no' and Q3-Q9 follow as 'no'.

notes: Full text appears complete, though some symbols, equations and numeric values (coordinates, R2 thresholds, p-values) are missing from the extraction. Single site, single cultivar, single sampling date, leaf-level laboratory measurements only.
